Gateway permissions on macOS

Optional Full Disk Access invitation and macOS permissions used by GateFox.

About 4 min read · 2 sections

On this page
01 Permissions for development work 02 Verification

The app offers an optional Full Disk Access invitation once, after the setup wizard closes or on the next launch of an already configured app. Open Full Disk Access opens System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access. Not now dismisses the invitation. Both choices are remembered in the current launch's preferences; explicit configuration launches retain their isolated preferences. Neither choice records an access grant.

Settings → Permissions always provides the same action. Enable GateFox manually in System Settings. If it is missing, use + to select the installed app; Show this app reveals the current bundle in Finder. An unbundled development executable has no app-reveal button. If a settings link cannot open, the panel gives the manual navigation path.

Full Disk Access permits broad access to protected data, including Mail, Messages, Safari data and backups. Ordinary development in accessible project folders does not require it. macOS has no public general-purpose API to request or reliably query this grant for the app and its separately running tools. The app does not probe private files or read the TCC database to guess status. Opening System Settings never produces a green permission indicator.

If macOS requests a quit and reopen, finish active work first. The control panel does not restart the service or tool processes. Verify the intended file action from its actual execution host after any required restart. The responsible identity can be the signed gateway runtime, a harness, a terminal, or an independent tool. Review the identity macOS reports instead of granting every installed executable access. Permissions on one Mac do not authorize another. See Node and tool permissions for the signed runtime and responsibility boundary.

Permissions for development work

The panel covers access used by GateFox and its client-run tasks. Additional permissions remain conditional on the actual action. Provider inference does not execute tools or acquire permissions on the caller's behalf.

Permission When it applies
Full Disk Access A development task needs protected files. Ordinary accessible project folders do not require it.
Automation A client-run task uses AppleScript or Apple Events to control another app. Run the intended action to trigger consent for the actual requesting app and target app.
Local Network The gateway connects to a configured model server or shared gateway on the LAN. Loopback-only use does not require it. macOS requests access when needed.

Other gateway permissions exposes Automation and Local Network links. The signed app and runtime already declare Automation and local-network use; opening a settings pane does not request consent for an unrelated action or target. The gateway does not request microphone, camera, Accessibility or Screen Recording permissions for itself as part of this flow. Independent client tools retain their own permission flows.

Apple's Privacy & Security settings guide describes the scope of each macOS grant and manually adding applications.

Verification

Run the source gate and npm run app:test. Native tests cover invitation deferral, explicit-answer persistence, isolated preferences, settings destinations, and failures that retain manual instructions.

On an unlocked Mac, launch an isolated app fixture and verify the invitation appears after setup. Dismiss it, relaunch, and confirm it stays dismissed while Settings still offers the controls. Open Full Disk Access and verify the actual pane, then inspect Automation and Local Network. Do not grant access or restart active work as part of routine UI verification. A successful URL-open callback proves dispatch only; rendered destinations and actual protected-file actions need separate desktop evidence.

On October 29, 2026, the build and type checks passed. The full source run passed 3,562 gateway tests and 160 Claude desktop checks, with one intentional skip in each suite. An earlier Unix-listener timeout passed both a targeted rerun and the full rerun. Native verification passed 119 tests and 87 packaging checks. The isolated app's Permissions panel was inspected visually, and its Full Disk Access and Automation actions opened the actual System Settings pages. No privacy grant or live gateway restart was performed. The production app has not been updated by this source verification.
